messages:
Alex: Heads-up — noticing queue climb in us-west-2 for low-priority GPU jobs starting ~03:10 UTC. Looks correlated with a recent keystore routing tweak that pinned certain requests to a small subnet. TL;DR: keystore affinity + strict sg rules -> QoS gradient where bursty workloads starve smaller pools. Anyone else seeing this?
Maria: Yep saw the same. Spike aligns with that keystore affinity rollout last night. latency p50 for small models jumped 2.3x.
TJ: confirmed in dashboards — fairshare drop for burstable tier nodes, autoscaler didn't trigger quickly because node tags mismatched the new allowlist.
Jun: quick question — is this purely routing/sg or did we also tighten audit export egress that could be blocking keystore traffic?
EMI: We tightened egress to the audit shipper in the eu->us rule set, but that shouldn't affect us-west-2 keystore path. However the SG change added a conditional deny for 10.0.64.0/18 which overlaps the warm pool.
Alex: So two factors: keystore affinity sharding + overly restrictive SG (cidr/sn overlap). That explains starvation. Can we do a short mitigation (30m) to unblock traffic while we plan a proper rollback?
Maria: Proposed quick fix: relax SG to allow 10.0.64.0/18 -> 10.0.0.0/16, and add explicit auditlog label on nodes to keep compliance records. I can run the change but want signoff.
TJ: +1 from me if we add a compensating audit log entry (we need traceability for the temporary exception). also, annotate the change in the inc-doc.
Jun: Also recommend throttling keystore affinity for the bursty tier rather than full pinning. That should reduce hot-spotting without opening SG wide.
EMI: I can push a policy tweak — change affinity weight from 100 -> 30 for burstable group. That will let routing spread.
Alex: Plan: (1) Maria loosens SG for 30m and adds an audit marker; (2) EMI lowers keystore affinity weight; (3) TJ watches fairshare and autoscaler; (4) Jun prepares a follow-up runbook to rework allowlists + rollout gating. Agree?
Maria: On it. Pasting command I'll run in case we need to revert quickly:
```bash
# add temporary sg ingress for warmpool overlap
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.64.0/18 --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=temporary-exception,Value=keystore-qos}]'
```
TJ: watching metrics now. p50 dropping back toward normal, request queue length halved in the last 4m. good sign.
deploy-bot: deploy: keystore-affinity-policy v2.1 -> staged to us-west-2 at 03:22 UTC :rocket:
EMI: Affinity weight change applied. Routing now spreads requests to 3 more pools.
Alex: Nice. Quick cost note — when these pools starve we fallback to larger instances in other regions and that added ~ $1.8k last 6h. If this becomes frequent it's ~ $54k/mo. tagging for finance.
Jun: I'll draft the postmortem section: root cause = affinity + sg overlap + tag drift; action items = allowlist consolidation, affinity gradual ramp, and add e2e test that simulates keystore routing under tag drift.
Maria: Logged the temporary exception and set a TTL of 30m. I left a comment with audit token: audit://tmp-exc/1709456789.
TJ: Can we add an alert for 'keystore-queue-gradient' with 5m burn to catch this earlier? Right now we only alert at 30m.
Alex: yes — add lower-sensitivity alert and tie to runbook that runs the three-step mitigation.
EMI: I'll open the PR for affinity ramp and a canary that validates fairshare distribution under tag loss.
Jun: thx all. followup: schedule a small blast test tomorrow in staging to ensure keystore affinity ramp doesn't regress.
Alex: Great work. Closing thread once we verify 20m stable. :thumbsup:
